# Help wanted

Specific things this study needs, by who can help. The same list, with buttons, is on the [project website](https://penpro.github.io/PUD-Feasibility/#help). Each item opens a pre-filled GitHub issue (free account needed). Before starting something big, open an **I'll take this on** issue so two people don't do the same work.

## Anyone

No expertise needed. Most of these take 15–30 minutes.

### A1. Find where the "$1.2–1.5 billion" price tag came from

*15 min · 🟠 high · OQ-07*

A price for buying PSE's Kitsap system keeps getting repeated, but we have not found the original source. A number this big needs a paper trail before anyone should use it.

1. If you saw it on a mailer, ad, website, social post or at a debate, post a photo or link.
2. Say when and where you saw it, and who it was attributed to.

## Kitsap homes & businesses

Your own electric bills are some of the best data we can get. No names, addresses or account numbers, ever.

### B1. Share a year of your home's electric use (no personal info)

*15 min · 🟠 high*

To compare bills fairly we need real usage patterns: homes heated by gas, by baseboard, by heat pump. Averages hide the differences that matter most to your bill.

1. From your PSE bills or online account, list 12 months of kWh used and the bill total each month.
2. Add your home type, heating type, rough size and town.
3. Never post your name, address or account number. The form tells you exactly what to include.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=usage-profile.md&title=%5BUsage%5D%20Home%2C%20%3Cheating%20type%3E%2C%20%3Ctown%3E)**

### B2. Businesses: share your yearly kWh and PSE rate schedule

*10 min · 🔴 most needed · OQ-03*

How much electricity Kitsap businesses use is the biggest single unknown in our estimate. Plausible values swing the county total by about 23%.

1. Post your annual kWh, your PSE rate schedule number (printed on the bill, e.g. Schedule 24, 25 or 26) and your type of business.
2. No business name needed.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=usage-profile.md&title=%5BUsage%5D%20Business%2C%20Schedule%20%3Cnumber%3E%2C%20%3Cbusiness%20type%3E)**

## Paper chasers

Public records and filings. It takes persistence, not expertise.

### C1. Find PSE's peak demand for Kitsap

*1–3 hours · 🔴 most needed · OQ-05*

Wires, substations and power contracts are sized for the highest-demand hour of the year. Our range is wide (342–738 MW) because Kitsap's real peak has not been published.

1. Start with PSE's request for proposals for "non-wires alternatives" in Kitsap County, and PSE's Integrated Resource Plan.
2. Then try a public records request to the Utilities and Transportation Commission (UTC) for Kitsap-area load studies.
3. Comment on the issue before filing anything, so two people don't file the same request.

- [PSE Kitsap non-wires RFP announcement](https://pse.com/press-release/details/Puget-Sound-Energy-issues-RFP-for-non-wires-alternatives-in-Kitsap-County)
- [WA Utilities and Transportation Commission](https://www.utc.wa.gov/)
- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20PSE%20Kitsap-area%20peak%20demand)**

### C2. Get the real kWh behind the county's climate report

*ongoing · 🔴 most needed · OQ-01, OQ-02, OQ-12*

The 2022 county climate report was built on actual electricity data from the utilities but published only emissions. That data would replace our best estimate with a measurement.

1. Records requests went to the state Department of Commerce and Kitsap County on Nov 4, 2026, 2:30 PM. By law each owes a first reply by Thu, Nov 12.
2. If you work with either agency and can share the data, or want to help follow up, say so on the issue.

- [The request as sent](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/blob/main/docs/records-requests/2026-11-04_kitsap-electricity-consumption.md)
- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=volunteer.md&title=%5BHelp%5D%20Records%20request%3A%20Kitsap%20kWh%20behind%20the%202022%20GHG%20report)**

### C3. Count the Kitsap customers of Mason PUD 3 and Peninsula Light

*1 hour · OQ-13*

Two other utilities serve edges of Kitsap County. Their customers would not be part of a PSE buyout, so we need to subtract them from county-wide numbers.

1. Mason PUD 3 is a public agency, so a records request works. Peninsula Light is a co-op, so just ask.
2. We need customers and yearly kWh inside Kitsap County, homes and businesses separately if possible.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20Kitsap%20customers%20of%20Mason%20PUD%203%20/%20Peninsula%20Light)**

### C4. Pull Jefferson PUD's paper trail

*1–2 hours · 🟠 high · OQ-11*

Jefferson County took over from PSE in 2013, the only recent Washington example. News stories say the price was $103 million and rose to about $109 million. We need the original documents, not the headlines.

1. Find the UTC order approving PSE's sale to Jefferson PUD.
2. Find Jefferson PUD's audited financial statements (State Auditor's Office) and bond documents (EMMA).
3. Post links with page numbers for the purchase price, adjustments, separation costs and financing.

- [WA State Auditor reports](https://sao.wa.gov/)
- [EMMA municipal bond documents](https://emma.msrb.org/)
- [WA Utilities and Transportation Commission](https://www.utc.wa.gov/)
- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20Jefferson%20PUD%20acquisition%20primary%20documents)**

### C5. How many PSE customers are in Kitsap, homes vs. businesses?

*1 hour · 🟠 high · OQ-03*

PSE says about 130,000 customers in Kitsap, a rounded number from a campaign-season press release. The split between homes and businesses changes the total a lot.

1. Look for Kitsap customer counts in PSE's UTC filings, community reports or franchise agreements with Kitsap cities.
2. Or ask PSE directly and post the reply.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20PSE%20Kitsap%20customers%20by%20class)**

## People who know utilities, finance or law

Point us to the rule, the filing or the page number.

### D1. How much cheap federal hydropower could a new PUD actually get?

*1–2 hours · 🔴 most needed · OQ-06*

This may be the biggest single factor in whether bills go up or down. PSE says a new PUD would start with none. KUOW reported that public utilities can get 200 megawatts. Both can't be fully right, so we need BPA's actual rules.

1. Find BPA's "Provider of Choice" policy and contract documents covering new public utilities.
2. Post the rule, the amount, the timeline, and the document and page number.

- [Bonneville Power Administration](https://www.bpa.gov/)
- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20BPA%20Tier%201%20rules%20for%20a%20new%20public%20utility)**

### D2. Do the Navy bases still buy power straight from BPA?

*30 min · OQ-04*

BPA's 2016 slides say the Bremerton and Bangor bases are served directly by BPA. If that is still true, they are not part of any takeover, and county-wide totals overstate what a PUD would serve.

1. Point us to a current BPA customer list, NAVFAC contract or other document confirming it.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20Naval%20Base%20Kitsap%20power%20supplier)**

### D3. What would bonds cost a brand-new electric PUD?

*1 hour*

Buying the system would be paid for with bonds. The interest rate, term and covenants drive a big part of any future bill.

1. Point us to official statements for recent Washington PUD revenue bonds (rate, term, rating, coverage).
2. If you work in municipal finance, tell us how a start-up utility would likely be rated.

- [EMMA municipal bond documents](https://emma.msrb.org/)
- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20Revenue%20bond%20terms%20for%20a%20new%20WA%20electric%20PUD)**

### D4. Line crews and storms: what does a 130,000-customer utility need?

*30–60 min · 🟠 high*

PSE says it has more than 70 employees and 50+ contractors working in Kitsap and can bring crews from across the West after storms. That is a fair question for any new utility, so we want to test it with real numbers.

1. If you've worked at a utility, share staffing levels, crew counts, mutual-aid setups and contractor use.
2. Or point us to PUD annual reports that publish them.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20Utility%20staffing%20/%20storm-response%20benchmarks)**

### D5. How are utility systems valued in a buyout or condemnation?

*1 hour*

If PSE would not sell, state law (RCW 54.16.020) allows a court process to set a fair price. How Washington courts have valued utility property shapes the cost range.

1. Point us to Washington cases, appraisal methods, or the costs of past condemnations, with citations.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=data-submission.md&title=%5BData%5D%20Utility%20valuation%20/%20condemnation%20precedent)**

## Data & code

Python, spreadsheets, a skeptical eye.

### E1. Build an hourly load shape from EIA-930

*a few hours · OQ-05*

Our monthly shape comes from billing data. Hourly grid data for PSE's area would show the true winter peak pattern and how often it happens.

1. Download EIA-930 hourly demand for the PSEI balancing authority.
2. Add the raw files and a reader in model/, following CONTRIBUTING.md (raw files untouched, registered in data/sources.yaml).

- [EIA Hourly Electric Grid Monitor](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/)
- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=volunteer.md&title=%5BHelp%5D%20EIA-930%20hourly%20load%20shape%20for%20PSEI)**

### E2. Challenge our guesses

*30 min*

Some inputs are labeled ASSUMPTION because nobody has measured them yet: future EV counts, how much homes switch from gas to electric heat. These are the first things to question.

1. Pick a parameter marked ASSUMPTION in model/config.yaml.
2. Propose a low / central / high and say what evidence supports it.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=challenge.md&title=%5BChallenge%5D%20)**

### E3. Check our math

*1 hour*

Every number here should be reproducible from public files. If you can't reproduce one, that's a bug.

1. Run the four commands in the README (verify sources, run the model, run the tests).
2. Read model/load.py. Report anything wrong, unclear or unsupported.

- **[Start: open a pre-filled issue](https://github.com/penpro/PUD-Feasibility/issues/new?template=correction.md&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20)**
